_comment: This document is the sole authority for what a render is ALLOWED to produce.
editorRender consults it before spawning, and editorValidateOutput measures
the produced file against it afterwards. Those are two different questions —
'did we ask for the right thing' and 'did we get it' — and they must not be
answered from two different tables, or a drifting encoder can satisfy one
Every numeric here is an INTEGER (ms, Hz, px, milli-dB, milli-LU) for the
same reason edit_policy_v1.json is: a float that round-trips differently in
two processes turns a deterministic identity into a flaky one.
NO SECRETS. This file is read by the worker, hashed into render evidence and
quoted in failure detail. A credential here would be persisted and logged.

_encoderComment: The encoder settings are part of the profile, not a render-time choice.
Two renders of one plan that differ only in CRF are not the same output,
and 'the operator picked a different preset that day' is not a thing the
audit trail should ever have to say.
_validationComment: What editorValidateOutput will accept from the produced file. The
duration tolerance is Gate-0 §4's ±250 ms and is NOT independently
chosen here — it is restated so the validator has one place to read it,
and renderCatalog.test.ts asserts it still equals the frozen value.

_fontComment: Fonts are named by BASENAME, never by absolute path: the path differs
between the container, the VPS and a developer machine, and a path baked
into a frozen catalog is a catalog that is wrong on two of the three.
The sha256 is what makes `render_font_integrity_failed` a real check rather
than a file-exists test. A substituted font renders captions that are
positioned differently from the ones the compiler measured — which is a
silent visual defect, exactly the class that survives a green test run.
sha256 null means 'this deployment has not pinned this font yet'. That is
recorded as UNPINNED and refused under strict integrity, never treated as
matching. An absent digest is not a passing digest.
_transitionComment: Crossfade bounds. Gate-0 §4 permits `restrained` only at a verified scene
boundary with handles on both sides; these numbers bound the overlap once
that has already been established. A transition longer than the shorter of
the two segments it joins would consume a whole piece, so the renderer
refuses it rather than producing a video with a segment that never appears.
_coverComment: The cover frame is extracted from the RENDERED OUTPUT at the plan's
outputTimeMs — never from the source at sourceTimeMs. They are the same
picture only if the time map is correct, and using the source would make
the cover unable to disagree with a broken map. It is the one artifact
positioned to catch that, so it is taken where it can.

_comment: Gate-0 §9 capacity thresholds, restated as enforcement. The render
timeout is derived from the max realtime ratio and the plan's own output
duration, so a 15-minute plan gets 6x its length and a 15-second plan
does not inherit a 90-minute budget it could hang inside.
